text: Quick update on the pricing page test (started Monday 2 weeks ago, 50/50 split). Control: 18,204 visitors, 731 signups. Variant with annual toggle: 18,110 visitors, 802 signups. I've been checking the dashboard every morning. Each signup is worth roughly $62 to us. We'd only bother shipping for a lift of 5% or more.

Checkout button test. Original: 40,000 sessions at 3.1% conversion. New green button: 39,800 sessions at 3.4%. Ran three weeks, looked at it once at the end.
We sent 80% of traffic to the old flow and 20% to the new one to limit risk. Old flow: 52,300 users, 4,915 purchases. New flow: 13,050 users, 1,302 purchases. Average order value $48.

Headline test with three versions. A (current): 9,900 visitors, 410 clicks. B (question headline): 10,050 visitors, 455 clicks. C (number headline): 9,980 visitors, 431 clicks. We mainly care about B.
Email subject line test: control 120,000 sends, 14,400 opens; variant 120,000 sends, 15,120 opens.
Day 10 of the paywall test. I've peeked about 6 times so far, sorry. Control 7,200 / 288 paid. Test 7,150 / 329 paid. Planned 50-50.
Plan said we need at least a 3% relative lift to justify the engineering. Results after 28 days: baseline 61,400 visitors and 2,456 conversions, challenger 61,900 visitors and 2,557 conversions.
Signup form test, 50/50. Control: 5,000 visitors, 600 signups. Shorter form: 5,000 visitors, 660 signups. A signup is worth $15. Ran one week.
Variant B: 2,210 conversions out of 31,000 (7.13%). Variant A (control): 2,050 out of 30,700 (6.68%).
The new onboarding looks way better, conversion went up a lot, and the team is excited. Can we ship it?
Test ran for 3 weeks with daily check-ins at standup. A: 15,400 visitors, 1,078 trials. B: 15,350 visitors, 1,151 trials.

Treatment had 12,040 users and 1,686 activations; control had 11,980 users and 1,557 activations. 50/50 assignment, 14 days.
We decided up front that anything under 0.5 percentage points isn't worth it. Control 20,000 / 1,000. New 20,000 / 1,090.
Started 50/50, then on day 4 marketing moved the split to 70/30 in favour of the new page. Totals after 12 days: old page 9,100 visitors, 455 leads; new page 13,400 visitors, 737 leads.
Banner test: control 45k impressions, 900 clicks; variant 44k impressions, 1,012 clicks. 50/50, 2 weeks.
Control converted at 4.0% and the variant at 4.6%. We had about the same traffic in each.
Upsell modal test: 6,400 users saw the old modal and 288 upgraded; 6,350 saw the new one and 343 upgraded. Upgrades are worth about $120 in first-year revenue. One-week test, single readout.
